Reproducing the R Journal paper examples with LUCIDus 3.1.0

Purpose

This document runs every code example from

Zhao Y, Jia Q, Goodrich JA, Conti DV (2024). LUCIDus: An R Package For Implementing Latent Unknown Clustering By Integrating Multi-omics Data (LUCID) With Phenotypic Traits. The R Journal 16/2, 4–26. (RJ-2024-012)

against the current package, to confirm that all of them still run.

Numeric results are not expected to match the paper. Version 3.1.0 corrects several values that earlier versions reported incorrectly — including the log-likelihood, the BIC, and the coding of the outcome coefficients. Wherever output legitimately differs, a short note explains why and points at the corresponding NEWS.md entry. Two of the paper’s examples (fit10 and fit12) did not run at all before 3.1.0.

Every chunk is set with error = TRUE, so a failure is displayed and the knit carries on rather than hiding the remaining examples. A status table at the end lists the outcome of each one.

Requirements

required_version <- "3.1.0"
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(LUCIDus))
installed <- as.character(utils::packageVersion("LUCIDus"))
cat("LUCIDus version loaded:", installed, "\n")
#> LUCIDus version loaded: 3.2.0
if (utils::compareVersion(installed, required_version) < 0) {
  warning(
    "This document targets LUCIDus >= ", required_version, " but version ",
    installed, " is loaded.\n",
    "Several examples below (fit10, fit12) abort on earlier versions.\n",
    "Install the corrected package first, e.g.:\n",
    "  R CMD INSTALL /Users/qiranjia19961112/Desktop/lucid3.1/LUCIDus-3.2.0"
  )
}

ggplot2 is needed for the BIC figure in Section 3.3 and visdat for the missingness plots in Section 3.6. Note that the paper calls ggplot() without ever loading ggplot2; that is added here.

library(ggplot2)   # not loaded in the paper, but required by its BIC figure
library(visdat)

Run configuration

The paper’s heaviest calls tune a 41-value penalty grid, run graphical lasso on 210 features, and draw 200 bootstrap replicates each. With full_grid: TRUE (the default) the arguments below are exactly those printed in the paper. Set full_grid: FALSE in the YAML header to re-knit quickly with coarser grids.

K_GRID     <- if (params$full_grid) 2:6                     else 2:4
RHO_G      <- if (params$full_grid) seq(0, 0.4, by = 0.01)  else c(0, 0.1, 0.2)
RHO_ZMU    <- if (params$full_grid) 5:10                    else c(5, 10)
RHO_ZCOV   <- if (params$full_grid) seq(0.1, 0.4, by = 0.1) else c(0.1, 0.4)
N_NOISE_HI <- if (params$full_grid) 200                     else 40
BOOT_R     <- if (params$full_grid) 200                     else 25

data.frame(
  argument   = c("K (fit8/tune_K)", "Rho_G (fit10)", "Rho_Z_Mu (fit11)",
                 "Rho_Z_Cov (fit11)", "noise features (fit13)", "R (boot1/boot2)"),
  paper      = c("2:6", "seq(0, 0.4, by = 0.01)", "5:10",
                 "seq(0.1, 0.4, by = 0.1)", "200", "200"),
  this_run   = c(deparse(K_GRID), sprintf("%d values, %g..%g", length(RHO_G),
                 min(RHO_G), max(RHO_G)), deparse(RHO_ZMU),
                 sprintf("%d values", length(RHO_ZCOV)), N_NOISE_HI, BOOT_R)
)
#>                 argument                   paper          this_run
#> 1        K (fit8/tune_K)                     2:6               2:6
#> 2          Rho_G (fit10)  seq(0, 0.4, by = 0.01) 41 values, 0..0.4
#> 3       Rho_Z_Mu (fit11)                    5:10              5:10
#> 4      Rho_Z_Cov (fit11) seq(0.1, 0.4, by = 0.1)          4 values
#> 5 noise features (fit13)                     200               200
#> 6        R (boot1/boot2)                     200               200

3.1 Fitting a LUCID model

Loading and organising the data

library(LUCIDus)
# load data
data("simulated_HELIX_data")
simulated_data <- simulated_HELIX_data
exposome <- as.matrix(simulated_data[["phenotype"]]$hs_hg_m_scaled)
colnames(exposome) <- "hs_hg_m_scaled"
methylomics <- simulated_data$methylome
ck18 <- as.matrix(simulated_data[["phenotype"]]$ck18_scaled)
colnames(ck18) <- "ck18_scaled"
ck18_cat <- ifelse(ck18 > mean(ck18), 1, 0)
covars <- c("hs_child_age_yrs_None","e3_sex_None")
covs <- simulated_data[["phenotype"]][covars]
covs$e3_sex_None <- ifelse(covs$e3_sex_None == "male", 1, 0)

fit1, fit2 — continuous and binary outcomes

# Fit a LUCID model with a continuous outcome
fit1 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics, Y = ck18, init_omic.data.model = NULL,
              lucid_model = "early", family = "normal", K = 2)
# MLE of the LUCID model
# fit1$res_Beta
# fit1$res_Mu
# fit1$res_Sigma
# fit1$res_Gamma
# IPs of the sample
# fit1$inclusion.p
# Fit LUCID model with a binary outcome
fit2 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics, Y = ck18_cat, init_omic.data.model = NULL,
              lucid_model = "early", family = "binary", K = 2)

A note beyond the paper text – fit1 is a plain R list, and every field on it is documented on ?estimate_lucid’s @return:

names(fit1)
#>  [1] "res_Beta"             "res_Mu"               "res_Sigma"           
#>  [4] "res_Gamma"            "K"                    "var.names"           
#>  [7] "init_omic.data.model" "likelihood"           "inclusion.p"         
#> [10] "family"               "select"               "useY"                
#> [13] "Z"                    "init_impute"          "init_par"            
#> [16] "Rho"                  "missing_summary"      "em_control"

fit3.1, fit3.2, fit4 — initialisation

# Fit LUCID model with spherical shape, equal volume
fit3.1 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics, Y = ck18,
                lucid_model = "early", family = "normal", K = 2,
                init_par = "mclust", init_omic.data.model = "EII")
# Fit LUCID model with random guess
fit3.2 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics, Y = ck18,
                lucid_model = "early", family = "normal", K = 2,
                init_par = "random")
# Fit LUCID model with ellipsoidal shape, varying volume, shape, and orientation
fit4 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics, Y = ck18,
              lucid_model = "early", family = "normal", K = 2,
              init_omic.data.model = "VVV")

fit5 — unsupervised LUCID

# Fit an unsupervised LUCID model
fit5 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics, Y = ck18, lucid_model = "early",
              family = "normal", K = 2, useY = FALSE)

fit6, fit7 — adjusting for covariates

# Include covariates as G to X covariates
fit6 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics, Y = ck18, lucid_model = "early", K = 2,
              family = "normal", CoG = covs)
# Include covariates as X to Y covariates
fit7 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics, Y = ck18, lucid_model = "early", K = 2,
              family = "normal", CoY = covs)

3.2 Interpreting LUCID

summary(fit1)

Differs from the paper, by design. Three things changed in 3.1.0:

  • The log-likelihood is now the observed-data log-likelihood of the fitted model. Version 3.0.3 printed -6721.801 for this fit; the correct value at 3.0.3’s own estimates is -6575.88.
  • The BIC inherited that error, and additionally counted K*M^2 covariance parameters instead of Eq 13’s K*M(M+1)/2.
  • The outcome coefficients are now genuinely reference-coded: an intercept equal to cluster 1’s level, plus explicit contrasts. The paper’s cluster2 = 0.504 was in fact cluster 2’s own mean, printed under a cluster1 = 0 heading as though it were a contrast. The real contrast between the two clusters is about 1.044.

The omics means and the exposure odds ratio should closely match the paper.

# summarize a simple lucid model with a continuous outcome
summary(fit1)
#>

plot(fit1) — Sankey diagrams

# Visualize LUCID model via a Sankey diagram
plot(fit1)
# Change the node color
plot(fit1, G_color = "yellow")
# Change the link color
plot(fit1, pos_link_color = "red", neg_link_color = "green")

3.3 Model selection and variable selection

fit8 — choosing K

BIC values differ from the paper’s Figure 4 for the reasons given above. The selected K should still be 2.

fit8 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics, Y = ck18, lucid_model = "early",
              family = "normal", K = K_GRID)
# Check the optimal K
fit8$K
#> [1] 2

tune_lucid() and the BIC figure

# Look into the tuning process in more detail
tune_K <- tune_lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics, Y = ck18, lucid_model = "early",
                     family = "normal", K = K_GRID)

  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  geom_text(hjust = -0.2)

fit10 — variable selection for G

This example did not run before 3.1.0. When exactly one exposure survived selection, lucid() carried the tuned Rho_G into the post-selection refit, where the lasso requires at least two exposures, and the call aborted with At least 2 exposure variables are needed for variable selection. The refit on selected features is now unpenalised.

# Variable selection for G
# Add 10 more noise variables to the exposome
noise <- matrix(rnorm(420 * 10), nrow = 420)
exposome_noise <- cbind(exposome, noise)
fit10 <- lucid(G = exposome_noise, Z = methylomics, Y = ck18,
               lucid_model = "early", family = "normal", K = 2,
               Rho_G = RHO_G, seed = 1008)
# Summary of optimal lucid model
# summary(fit10)

fit11 — variable selection for Z

# Variable selection for Z
# add 10 more noise variables to the methylomics
methylomics_noise <- cbind(methylomics, noise)
fit11 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics_noise, Y = ck18,
               lucid_model = "early", family = "normal", K = 2,
               Rho_Z_Mu = RHO_ZMU, Rho_Z_Cov = RHO_ZCOV, seed = 1008)
# Summary of optimal lucid model
# summary(fit11)

fit12 — joint selection for G and Z

Also affected by the refit defect above; this example likewise did not complete before 3.1.0.

# Variable selection for G and Z jointly
fit12 <- lucid(G = exposome_noise, Z = methylomics_noise, Y = ck18,
               lucid_model = "early", family = "normal", K = 2,
               Rho_G = 0.01, Rho_Z_Mu = 10, Rho_Z_Cov = 0.5, seed = 123)

fit13 — high-dimensional Z

# Variable selection for Z (high number of features M)
set.seed(1008)
# Add 200 more noise features to the methylomics
noise <- matrix(rnorm(420 * N_NOISE_HI), nrow = 420)
methylomics_noise <- cbind(methylomics, noise)
fit13 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics_noise, Y = ck18,
               family = "normal", lucid_model = "early", K = 2,
               Rho_Z_Mu = 20, Rho_Z_Cov = 0.6)
# Summary of optimal lucid model
# summary(fit13)

3.4 Deriving confidence intervals

In 3.1.0 the bootstrap point estimate t0 is taken from the model you supply rather than from a refit under a fresh random seed, so the estimate column below now agrees with summary(fit1). Failed replicates are also counted and warned about instead of being silently dropped.

# Bootstrap to obtain 95% CI (by default) for LUCID
set.seed(123)
boot1 <- boot_lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics, Y = ck18,
                    model = fit1, R = BOOT_R)
# 90% CIs
boot2 <- boot_lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics, Y = ck18,
                    model = fit1, R = BOOT_R, conf = 0.9)

The paper prints this call as summary(fit1, boot.se = boot1)), which has an unbalanced closing parenthesis and is a typo in the article. Corrected here:

3.5 Prediction

Now matches the paper for the first time. The article prints table(pred1$pred.x) with labels 1 and 2, but the shipped code returned 0 and 1 in both 3.0.3 and pre-fix 3.1.0. Cluster labels are now 1..K throughout, consistent with Eq 21, summary(), and the inclusion.p columns. The counts themselves will differ from the paper’s 223/197.

# Predict cluster with information of Y
pred1 <- predict_lucid(model = fit1, G = exposome, Z = methylomics, Y = ck18)
# Predict cluster without information of Y
pred2 <- predict_lucid(model = fit1, G = exposome, Z = methylomics)
# Predicted cluster label
table(pred1$pred.x)
#> 
#>   1   2 
#> 236 184
# Predicted outcome
pred1$pred.y[1:5]
#> [1]  0.2453113 -0.3834012  0.2263823  0.4217217 -0.2095583

3.6 Incorporating missingness in multi-omics data

Two quirks in the paper’s own setup are reproduced verbatim rather than corrected, so that this section matches the article:

  • arrayInd(sample(1000, 0.1 * 1000), dim(methylomics)) draws from the first 1000 of the 4200 cells in methylomics, so the realised sporadic missingness rate is about 2.4%, not the 10% the expression suggests.
  • methylomics_miss_listwise[sample(1:100, 30), ] selects list-wise rows only from the first 100 of 420 observations.
library(visdat)
set.seed(1)
methylomics_miss_sporadic <- methylomics_miss_listwise <- as.matrix(methylomics)
index <- arrayInd(sample(1000, 0.1 * 1000), dim(methylomics))
methylomics_miss_sporadic[index] <- NA # sporadic missing pattern
methylomics_miss_listwise[sample(1:100, 30), ] <- NA # listwise missing pattern
vis_miss(as.data.frame(methylomics_miss_sporadic))

vis_miss(as.data.frame(methylomics_miss_listwise))

fit14 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics_miss_listwise, Y = ck18,
               lucid_model = "early", K = 2, family = "normal")
fit15 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = methylomics_miss_sporadic, Y = ck18,
               lucid_model = "early", K = 2, family = "normal")
# summary(fit15)

A check the paper does not perform — that list-wise rows are returned as NA rather than filled with fabricated values, and that observed cells are never altered:

lw <- which(rowSums(is.na(methylomics_miss_listwise)) == ncol(methylomics_miss_listwise))
cat("list-wise rows still NA in fit14$Z:      ", all(is.na(fit14$Z[lw, ])), "\n")
#> list-wise rows still NA in fit14$Z:       TRUE
obs <- !is.na(methylomics_miss_sporadic)
cat("observed cells unchanged in fit15$Z:     ",
    isTRUE(all.equal(fit15$Z[obs], methylomics_miss_sporadic[obs])), "\n")
#> observed cells unchanged in fit15$Z:      TRUE
cat("sporadic cells imputed and finite:       ",
    all(is.finite(fit15$Z[!obs])), "\n")
#> sporadic cells imputed and finite:        TRUE

3.7 LUCID in Parallel

summary(fit)$BIC now resolves for parallel and serial models; it was previously an early-model-only field that returned NULL elsewhere.

# Create a list of multi-omics data
omics_lst <- simulated_data[-which(names(simulated_data) == "phenotype")]
Z = omics_lst[c(1:3)]
# LUCID in parallel, adjusting for the covariates for the E-X and X-Y associations
fit16 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = Z, Y = ck18, K = list(2, 2, 2), family = "normal",
               CoY = covs, CoG = covs,
               lucid_model = "parallel", useY = TRUE)
# print the summary of the LUCID in parallel model

Beyond the paper text: fit16’s object structure. Two fields differ from fit1 above – N (sample size) is present here but not for early, and z (the joint E-step responsibility array across layers, before it is marginalized into inclusion.p) appears only for parallel.

               lucid_model = "parallel", useY = TRUE)

3.8 LUCID in Serial

# LUCID in serial, adjusting for the covariates of the E-X and X-Y associations

               lucid_model = "serial", CoY = covs, CoG = covs,

Beyond the paper text: fit18’s object structure. Serial adds submodel (the fitted stage models, each a complete early_lucid/lucid_parallel object) and res_Delta (between-stage transition coefficients). likelihood and select are present, same as early/parallel, but are aggregates over stages: likelihood sums each stage’s own log-likelihood (a serial chain has no single joint EM loop to report one from), and select is stage 1’s own selection only – the one stage whose G is the cohort’s real exposures, not a previous stage’s cluster probabilities.

names(fit18)
#>  [1] "res_Beta"             "res_Mu"               "res_Sigma"           
#>  [4] "res_Delta"            "res_Gamma"            "K"                   
#>  [7] "N"                    "var.names"            "init_omic.data.model"
#> [10] "inclusion.p"          "family"               "useY"                
#> [13] "Z"                    "init_impute"          "init_par"            
#> [16] "submodel"             "missing_summary"      "Rho"                 
#> [19] "em_control"           "likelihood"           "select"
cat("top-level likelihood (sum over stages):", fit18$likelihood, "\n")
#> top-level likelihood (sum over stages): -16192.84
cat("top-level select is stage 1's select:",
    identical(fit18$select, fit18$submodel[[1]]$select), "\n")
#> top-level select is stage 1's select: TRUE
# LUCID in serial with the first sub-model being LUCID in parallel
# and the second sub-model being LUCID early integration
# Rearrange the omics list to match the new structure of the LUCID in serial model
Z_new = list(list(omics_lst$methylome, omics_lst$transcriptome), omics_lst$miRNA)
# Fit the LUCID in serial model with the new omics list and the new K list
fit19 <- lucid(G = exposome, Z = Z_new, Y = ck18,
               lucid_model = "serial", CoY = covs, CoG = covs,
               K = list(list(2, 2), 2), useY = TRUE, family = "normal")
